\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اسب} (asb)}{اسب (asb)}]{\fa{اسب} (asb) — a horse}

\label{lesson:FA-C55-asb}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a dog, then the Persian for a cat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اسب}}
\textbf{\fa{اسب}} — \emph{asb} — \textquotedblleft{}a horse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{asb} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{asp}, \textquotedblleft{}horse\textquotedblright{}. Latin \emph{equus} is the same Indo-European word.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گوسفند} (gusfand)}{گوسفند (gusfand)}]{\fa{گوسفند} (gusfand) — a sheep}

\label{lesson:FA-C55-gusfand}

Before the new one: say the Persian for a cow, then the Persian for a goat.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گوسفند}}
\textbf{\fa{گوسفند}} — \emph{gusfand} — \textquotedblleft{}a sheep\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gusfand} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed: it continues Middle Persian \emph{gōspand}, \textquotedblleft{}sheep, small cattle\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). EtymDB traces it to an Avestan phrase meaning \textquotedblleft{}beneficent cattle\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پرنده} (parande)}{پرنده (parande)}]{\fa{پرنده} (parande) — a bird}

\label{lesson:FA-C55-parande}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a goat, then the Persian for a sheep.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پرنده}}
\textbf{\fa{پرنده}} — \emph{parande} — \textquotedblleft{}a bird\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{parande} is the \textquotedblleft{}-ing\textquotedblright{} form of \emph{paridan}, \textquotedblleft{}to fly\textquotedblright{}: \textquotedblleft{}a flying one\textquotedblright{}. The verb is built on \emph{par}, \textquotedblleft{}wing, feather\textquotedblright{}, a native word usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{parr}.
\end{cousinweb}
